name: presentation-quality-harness-candidates
purpose: Track open-source harnesses and benchmark ideas that can improve repeatable quality checks for presentation-agent deck specs, HTML decks, PPTX outputs, and future prompt-driven generation.

reader_guide.summary: Use this file before adding or installing any new presentation quality harness. It separates immediate no-install checks from optional browser/accessibility checks and later LLM/agent evaluation harnesses.
how_to_read: Read adoption_lanes first to decide whether the current task needs static, browser, visual, LLM, or benchmark-inspired evaluation.
Read candidates for each tool's fit, maturity signal, adoption status, and installation posture.
Read adoption_gates before any dependency installation or CI integration.
Treat community stars and discussion activity as discovery signals, not proof that a tool is correct for this project.
update_triggers: A new deck renderer, PPTX exporter, or prompt-driven generation path is added.
The project starts using browser screenshots, accessibility scans, or visual regression baselines.
A harness candidate is installed, rejected, or promoted into a workflow.
New slide-generation evaluation research becomes relevant.

structure_rules.rule: Do not install a harness merely because it is listed here; installation requires a project-local dependency decision, license/security review, verification plan, and rollback path.
structure_rules.reason: The user wants useful open source adoption without unnecessary dependency sprawl.

structure_rules.rule: Prefer deterministic no-install deck-spec and metadata checks before browser, visual, or LLM-judge checks.
structure_rules.reason: Static checks are faster, cheaper, and less flaky for early presentation-agent workflows.

structure_rules.rule: Screenshot baselines require a fixed browser, OS/font, viewport, and update policy before being treated as blocking tests.
structure_rules.reason: Visual diff tools can become noisy when host rendering differs.

structure_rules.rule: Use slide-generation papers and benchmarks as taxonomy sources first; do not treat their metrics as direct project acceptance criteria until reproduced locally.
structure_rules.reason: The project generates local HTML/PPT artifacts with different constraints than public benchmark datasets.

field_guide.meaning: Evaluation categories from immediate static checks through later LLM or benchmark-inspired checks.
Tool or research candidates with fit, risks, adoption timing, and installation posture.
Conditions that must be satisfied before a candidate becomes part of normal validation.
Ordered actions for applying the research to presentation-agent.

adoption_lanes.label: Static deck-spec quality
checks: required deck metadata and slide fields
slide count and layout family coverage
text density and title length guardrails
remote asset and unknown-license asset guardrails

adoption_lanes.label: Browser render and accessibility
checks: HTML opens at desktop and mobile-like viewports
slides are nonblank and keyboard navigation works
axe-core scan catches common contrast, label, duplicate-id, and aria issues

adoption_lanes.label: Visual regression
checks: stable screenshot baseline per deck template
explicit approval path for snapshot updates
dynamic elements hidden or normalized before screenshots

candidates.notes: Implement as a small Python module next to html_deck.py so it can run in unit tests and workspace-health without browser setup.

Installed project-locally in presentation-agent with @playwright/test 1.60.0 and Chromium v1223. Used for generated HTML deck desktop/mobile render, navigation, nonblank slide, controls, progress, and presenter notes checks. Visual baselines still need fixed environment rules.

Installed project-locally as @axe-core/playwright 4.11.3 and run inside the Playwright browser test. Automated scans catch common accessibility issues but must be paired with manual review for slide readability and narrative quality.
Good candidate once deck brief, script-generation prompt, and expected JSON contracts become repeatable test cases.
Pytest-like style could match this repo, but LLM-as-judge cost and API-key requirements should stay optional.
Most valuable if presentation-agent becomes an agentic workflow with datasets, solvers, scorers, and sandboxed tool use.
Useful as a pattern for dataset plus eval class design; direct adoption is not necessary for static presentation quality checks.
Use content, design, and coherence dimensions to shape local deck quality rubrics.
Useful for slide design flaw categories and for cautioning that automated slide critique is imperfect.
Use binary checklist idea for task-specific deck acceptance criteria; do not import benchmark claims as local guarantees.
Useful for future agents that operate browsers or desktop apps; not directly useful for current static HTML/PPT deck generation.

adoption_gates: Write a no-install static deck quality harness before adding browser dependencies.

Playwright and axe-core installation now has an audit record under _history/installations/2026/2026-06-01-presentation-agent-playwright.ko.md; future upgrades still require a new installation audit or update record.
Before visual regression becomes blocking, define viewport, browser, font, OS, snapshot update, and false-positive handling rules.
Before LLM harness adoption, define deterministic prompt inputs, expected output contracts, cost controls, API-key handling, and evaluator disagreement policy.
Before using benchmark-inspired rubrics as acceptance criteria, translate them into local deck-specific checks and run a manual sanity review.

recommended_next_steps.action: Add a Python no-install deck quality harness for deck-spec JSON.
recommended_next_steps.reason: It gives immediate repeatable value without dependency sprawl.

recommended_next_steps.action: Maintain Playwright plus axe-core browser smoke tests and run them after generated HTML deck changes.
recommended_next_steps.reason: Generated HTML decks now have project-local Chromium render, navigation, responsive, and accessibility checks.

recommended_next_steps.action: Convert PPTAgent, SlideAudit, and PresentBench ideas into a local presentation rubric.
recommended_next_steps.reason: The project needs local criteria that separate factual grounding, narrative quality, and visual design flaws.

recommended_next_steps.action: Evaluate promptfoo or DeepEval only after prompt-driven generation becomes repeatable.
recommended_next_steps.reason: LLM eval tools are useful for prompt drift, but premature before stable prompt contracts exist.
